notes: RULE 3 CHECK - catalogue is LIVE. Swoon Editions went through a pre-pack administration in Dec 2019 (co-founders bought the business back) but continues to trade under the same name; Companies House shows SWOON EDITIONS LTD active, and the site's own sitemap (https://www.swooneditions.com/media/sitemap.xml) carries lastmod dates up to 2026-07-30, with live Klarna checkout, live stock status and a working cart. So this is a real, current catalogue, not a shutdown. ACCESS ROUTE: the storefront is a client-side React SPA (empty #root in the HTML) so plain curl and WebFetch both return only the shell. The site is Magento 2 behind it and exposes an unauthenticated GraphQL endpoint at https://www.swooneditions.com/graphql (POST) - that is the site's own data layer and it answered every query directly with no impersonation, proxy or interstitial work needed. The category tree came from `{categories(pageSize:400,currentPage:N,filters:{})}` paged 3x to cover all 1114 nodes, cross-checked against the sitemap and against the rendered mega-menu (obtained via r.jina.ai, which renders the SPA nav but lazy-loads the product grid). COUNT VERIFICATION (Rule 1): the storefront publishes NO rendered 'N products' header anywhere - there is no count in the mega-menu, on the category landing pages or on the listing grids. So the only available number is the Magento total. The brief flags Magento `categoryList.product_count` as measured-inflated (169 vs 43 live), so I did not use it unchecked: for every row I ran `{products(pageSize:60,filter:{category_id:{eq:"ID"}}){total_count items{...}}}` and enumerated the category to exhaustion. In all 16 categories tested the returned item array length exactly equalled `total_count` (e.g. Mirrors: total_count 26, 26 distinct product items returned), and the Lighting children summed exactly to the Lighting parent (3+1+2+1+0 = 7). `product_count` and the live `products.total_count` also agreed on every node here, so on this store the Magento total survives the exhaustion check. Counts were read twice ~20 min apart with zero drift. SCOPE - Swoon is furniture-led, so the in-scope list is genuinely short, as anticipated. EXCLUDED and why: Sofas, Chairs, Tables, Storage, Beds, Footstools, Desks, Kitchen (cat 201 = kitchen furniture, no tableware or glassware), Bespoke furniture, Outdoor Furniture - all furniture. Rugs (1), Curtains (2), Cushions (0), Bedding (0), and the Piglet throws/napkin sitting loose in Accessories - textiles. 'Speedy lighting' (6) and 'Speedy accessories' (7) - delivery-speed facets, not product categories. Style branches (Art deco, Mid-century, Industrial, Classic, Contemporary, Scandi) including their /lighting and /accessories children - pure style re-cuts, and every one of their lighting nodes is empty (0) anyway. New In, Bestsellers, Clearance, Refurbished, Flash SALE, Collections, Look Book, Editions, Range, Delivery by Christmas, Almost/Not Perfect, Gift cards, Swatches, 'Test & Utility cat' - marketing/nav/internal, never extractable. MIRROR SUB-NODES DROPPED AS PROVEN FACET RE-CUTS: the mega-menu offers Brass mirrors (4), Rectangle mirrors (14), Hexagon mirrors (0) and Round mirrors (4) under Mirrors. I compared product-ID sets rather than names: they sum to 22 against a parent of 26, they overlap each other (lark-luxe-round-mirror-silver-mirror-black-steel appears in BOTH Brass mirrors and Round mirrors), and Round mirrors even contains a non-mirror (harpenden-scandi-floating-dressing-table). They are shape/material filters over the same 26 mirrors, so Mirrors is emitted as a single leaf carrying the authoritative 26. RULE 0.6 OVERLAP DOCUMENTED: Swoon presents both a product-type Lighting tree and room-cut lighting nodes, so both are emitted. The three room lighting rows (Bedroom 3, Dining Room 3, Home Office 4) are drawn entirely from the same 7 products as the type tree - Cusp floor lamp, Lattu table lamp, Fanny wall light, Marbella table lamp - but they are genuine separate nav branches under their room parents, not filters, so per Rule 0.6 both branches are emitted and the overlap is stated here rather than resolved by dropping. ROOM 'ACCESSORIES' NODES DROPPED, AND NOT BECAUSE OF THE ROOM WORD: hallway/accessories (26) returns the byte-for-byte identical 26-product population as accessories/mirrors - the same listing under a second URL, which Rule 0.6 explicitly still allows dropping. living-room/accessories (32), bedroom/accessories (31) and study/accessories (5) are mirrors plus rugs, curtains, ottomans, footstools and a mattress - mixed roll-ups whose only decorative content is the Mirrors row already captured, so they were dropped under 'mixed roll-ups: drop them, don't pad', on product type, not on the room word. SWOON SELECTS IS DEFUNCT: the site retains a large third-party marketplace subtree (swoon-selects/*) with exactly the categories this brief wants - Clocks, Wall art, Dinnerware (Bowls, Plates, Mugs & Cups, Serveware, Vases & Jugs), Bathroom accessories, and four separate lighting brand ranges (houseof, Nove, Vintlux). Every one of those nodes now returns 0 products; the only non-zero remnants are a single pendant light and a single napkin. It is a retired section, so no rows were emitted for it - but it is worth flagging that Swoon's decor range used to be much broader than what is live today. Lamp shades is kept as a row at a verified qty of 0: it is a live node in the /lighting sub-nav and 0 is the exact, empty-but-real answer. All category names kept pure ASCII with no GBP sign.
